source.text: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς πολλοὺς ὄχλους περὶ αὐτὸν ἐκέλευσεν ἀπελθεῖν εἰς τὸ πέραν.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the Jesus many crowds around him he ordered to depart to the other side.

en.L: Now when Jesus saw great crowds around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave orders to go over to the other side.
en.B: When Jesus saw the crowds gathering around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave orders to cross to the other side of the lake.
en.R: Jesus saw the big crowd around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to cross over to the other side of the lake.

fr.L: Or Jésus, voyant de grandes foules autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, donna l’ordre de passer sur l’autre rive.
fr.B: Quand Jésus vit les foules se rassembler autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donna l’ordre de passer sur l’autre rive du lac.
fr.R: Jésus a vu la grande foule autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples de traverser le lac pour aller sur l’autre rive.

decisions.choice: the other side: the east shore of the Sea of Galilee
alternatives: the far side of a river
decisions.reason: From Capernaum, the other side was the largely Gentile region of the Decapolis (8:28).

decisions.choice: of the lake (B, R); his followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what is crossed; Readable says whom he told.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("il leur dit", "Jésus lui dit")
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers now meet stories. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level. Readable says "disciples" where the English Readable says "followers", as the style guide keeps "les disciples" at every level.

source.text: καὶ προσελθὼν εἷς γραμματεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ἀκολουθήσω σοι ὅπου ἐὰν ἀπέρχῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And having come one scribe said to him, Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.

en.L: And a scribe came and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, I will follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wherever {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go."
en.B: A scribe came up and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, I will follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wherever {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go."
en.R: A teacher of the law came to Jesus and said, "Teacher, I will follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} anywhere {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go."

fr.L: Et un scribe s’approcha et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Maître, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} suivrai partout où {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} iras. »
fr.B: Un scribe s’approcha et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Maître, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} suivrai partout où {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} iras. »
fr.R: Un spécialiste de la Loi est venu voir Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Maître, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} suivrai n’importe où, partout où {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} iras. »

decisions.choice: Teacher: a title of respect for a rabbi
decisions.reason: In Matthew outsiders and opponents call Jesus "Teacher" (12:38; 22:16), while disciples say "Lord" (8:21). The difference may hint that the scribe does not yet understand who Jesus is.

decisions.choice: a teacher of the law
decisions.reason: As in 2:4.

decisions.choice: un scribe (L, B), un spécialiste de la Loi (R); Maître for "Teacher"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms for the scribes. French addresses a teacher of disciples as "Maître", as in the French of Mark 4:38; "Enseignant" is not used as a form of address.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Αἱ ἀλώπεκες φωλεοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνώσεις, ὁ δὲ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἔχει ποῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν κλίνῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And says to him the Jesus, The foxes holes have and the birds of the heaven nests, the but Son of the Man not has where the head he may lay.

en.L: And Jesus says to him, "Foxes have holes and the birds of the sky [have] nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head."
en.B: Jesus told him, "Foxes have their holes and the birds in the sky their nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to rest {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head."
en.R: Jesus said to him, "Foxes have holes to live in, and birds have nests. But the Son of Man has no home where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can lie down to rest."

fr.L: Et Jésus lui dit : « Les renards ont des tanières et les oiseaux du ciel des nids, mais le Fils de l’homme n’a pas où poser {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête. »
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « Les renards ont leurs terriers et les oiseaux du ciel leurs nids, mais le Fils de l’homme n’a pas d’endroit où reposer {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête. »
fr.R: Jésus lui a dit : « Les renards ont des trous pour vivre, et les oiseaux ont des nids. Mais le Fils de l’homme n’a pas de maison où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} peut se coucher pour se reposer. »

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's way of speaking of himself
decisions.reason: This is the first time the title appears in Matthew. It is Jesus's own way of naming himself. In Hebrew and Aramaic "son of man" means a human being, and in Daniel 7:13-14 "one like a son of man" receives everlasting dominion from God. Jesus uses it of his lowliness (here), his suffering (17:22) and his coming in glory (24:30).

decisions.choice: nowhere to lay his head: following Jesus means sharing his homeless life
alternatives: Jesus was poor in every sense
decisions.reason: Jesus had a base in Capernaum (4:13), but his ministry kept him moving. The scribe must count the cost.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man, with capitals as a title
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the phrase as a title for himself, so it is capitalized.

decisions.choice: le Fils de l’homme, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: a title, kept in its familiar French form at every level, with the capital on "Fils" only.

source.text: ἕτερος δὲ τῶν μαθητῶν εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι πρῶτον ἀπελθεῖν καὶ θάψαι τὸν πατέρα μου.

records.literal_gloss: Another then of the disciples said to him, Lord, allow me first to go and to bury the father of me.

en.L: And another of the disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father."
en.B: Another of the disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, allow me first to go away and bury my father."
en.R: Another of Jesus's followers said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, let me first go and bury my father."

fr.L: Et un autre des disciples {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Seigneur, permets-moi d’aller d’abord enterrer mon père. »
fr.B: Un autre, parmi les disciples, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Seigneur, permets-moi d’abord de m’en aller enterrer mon père. »
fr.R: Un autre disciple de Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Seigneur, laisse-moi d’abord aller enterrer mon père. »

decisions.choice: bury my father: the most sacred duty a son owed his parents
decisions.reason: Burying one's parents was a duty that came before many religious obligations (Tobit 4:3). The father may have just died, or the son may mean staying until he dies.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι, καὶ ἄφες τοὺς νεκροὺς θάψαι τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus says to him, Follow me, and leave the dead to bury the of themselves dead.

en.L: But Jesus says to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and let the dead bury their own dead."
en.B: But Jesus told him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Leave the dead to bury their own dead."
en.R: But Jesus said to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} now. Let those who are dead to God bury their own dead."

fr.L: Mais Jésus lui dit : « Suis-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et laisse les morts enterrer leurs propres morts. »
fr.B: Mais Jésus lui répondit : « Suis-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Laisse les morts enterrer leurs morts. »
fr.R: Mais Jésus lui a dit : « Suis-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} maintenant. Laisse ceux qui sont morts aux yeux de Dieu enterrer leurs morts. »

decisions.choice: let the dead bury their own dead: let those without the life of the kingdom see to it
decisions.reason: The saying is shocking on purpose. The first "dead" are most likely the spiritually dead, those who do not follow Jesus. Nothing comes before the call to follow him (10:37).

decisions.choice: those who are dead to God
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense of the first "dead", which the meaning note marks as uncertain.

decisions.choice: ceux qui sont morts aux yeux de Dieu (R)
alternatives: ceux qui sont morts pour Dieu
decisions.reason: "Morts pour Dieu" would mean in French that they had died for God's sake. "Aux yeux de Dieu" gives the likely sense of the English "dead to God", which the meaning note marks as uncertain (m1).

source.text: Καὶ ἐμβάντι αὐτῷ εἰς πλοῖον ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having entered he into a boat followed him the disciples of him.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into the boat, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Then Jesus stepped into the boat, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then Jesus got into a boat, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut monté dans la barque, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivirent.
fr.B: Puis Jésus monta dans la barque, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivirent.
fr.R: Ensuite Jésus est monté dans un bateau, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples sont partis avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

decisions.choice: followed him: the word for discipleship, after 8:19-22
decisions.reason: Matthew has just told of two would-be followers. Now the disciples follow Jesus into the boat and into the storm.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced names Jesus.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ σεισμὸς μέγας ἐγένετο ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, ὥστε τὸ πλοῖον καλύπτεσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων, αὐτὸς δὲ ἐκάθευδεν.

records.literal_gloss: And behold, a shaking great arose in the sea, so that the boat to be covered by the waves, he but was sleeping.

en.L: And look, a great shaking arose on the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was sleeping.
en.B: Without warning a great storm broke over the lake, and waves were sweeping over the boat. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was asleep.
en.R: Suddenly a very strong storm came on the lake. The waves were so big that water was coming into the boat. But Jesus was sleeping.

fr.L: Et voici, une grande secousse se produisit sur la mer, si bien que la barque était couverte par les vagues ; mais {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dormait.
fr.B: Soudain, une violente tempête s’abattit sur le lac, et les vagues passaient par-dessus la barque. Mais {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dormait.
fr.R: Tout à coup, une tempête très forte s’est levée sur le lac. Les vagues étaient si hautes que l’eau entrait dans le bateau. Mais Jésus dormait.

decisions.choice: a great shaking: a violent storm
decisions.reason: The word usually means an earthquake; here it is a storm that shook the sea. Matthew uses the same word for the shakings of the last days and of Jesus's death and rising (24:7; 27:54; 28:2).

decisions.choice: he was sleeping: rest that shows complete trust
alternatives: he did not know of the danger
decisions.reason: Sleeping in danger is a sign of trust in God (Psalm 3:6; 4:9).

decisions.choice: look (L); without warning (B); suddenly (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: voici (L) (for the whole passage); la mer (L), le lac (B, R); la barque (L, B), le bateau (R)
decisions.reason: As in the French of Mark 4-5: Literal keeps the Greek "sea", while Balanced and Readable say "lac", as the English Balanced and Readable say "lake", since the Sea of Galilee is a lake. French "voici" is still current for pointing to what follows, so Literal keeps it where English Literal says "look".

source.text: καὶ προσελθόντες ἤγειραν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Κύριε, σῶσον, ἀπολλύμεθα.

records.literal_gloss: And having come they woke him saying, Lord, save, we are perishing.

en.L: And they came and woke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Lord, save [us]; we are perishing!"
en.B: They came and woke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "Lord, save us!" they cried. "We are about to die!"
en.R: The followers went to Jesus and woke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up. They said, "Lord, save us! We are going to die!"

fr.L: Et s’étant approchés, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} réveillèrent, disant : « Seigneur, sauve[-nous], nous périssons ! »
fr.B: Ils vinrent {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} réveiller. « Seigneur, sauve-nous ! crièrent-ils. Nous allons mourir ! »
fr.R: Les disciples sont allés vers Jésus et ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont réveillé. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont dit : « Seigneur, sauve-nous ! Nous allons mourir ! »

decisions.choice: Lord, save: a cry for rescue, in the words of prayer
decisions.reason: The words echo the Psalms' cries to God (Psalm 69:2; 107:28).

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί δειλοί ἐστε, ὀλιγόπιστοι;

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, Why fearful are you, little-faiths?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Why are you afraid, you of little faith?"
en.B: He said to them, "Why are you so frightened, you who have so little faith?"
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Why are you so afraid? Your faith is so small!"

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Pourquoi êtes-vous craintifs, gens de peu de foi ? »
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Pourquoi avez-vous si peur, vous qui avez si peu de foi ? »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Pourquoi avez-vous si peur ? Votre foi est si petite ! »

decisions.choice: little faith: trust that gives way under pressure
decisions.reason: As in 6:30, the word rebukes disciples whose faith is real but weak.

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: gens de peu de foi (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek is one adjective, "little-faiths", with no word for men; "gens de peu de foi" keeps the compact address without adding "hommes".

source.text: τότε ἐγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τοῖς ἀνέμοις καὶ τῇ θαλάσσῃ, καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη μεγάλη.

records.literal_gloss: Then having arisen he rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a calm great.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got up and spoke sharply to the winds and the waves, and everything became completely calm.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got up and gave a command to the wind and the waves. The wind stopped, and the lake became very calm.

fr.L: Alors, s’étant levé, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} réprimanda les vents et la mer, et il se fit un grand calme.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se leva, parla durement aux vents et aux vagues, et tout devint parfaitement calme.
fr.R: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est levé et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a donné un ordre au vent et aux vagues. Le vent s’est arrêté, et le lac est devenu très calme.

decisions.choice: he rebuked the winds and the sea: what God does in the Psalms
decisions.reason: God rebukes the sea and stills the storm (Psalm 106:9; 107:29). Jesus does what Scripture says God does.

decisions.choice: spoke sharply to (B); gave a command to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the rebuke for a reader who may not expect it of weather.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἄνθρωποι ἐθαύμασαν λέγοντες· Ποταπός ἐστιν οὗτος ὅτι καὶ οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ ἡ θάλασσα αὐτῷ ὑπακούουσιν;

records.literal_gloss: The but men marveled saying, What sort is this one that even the winds and the sea him obey?

en.L: And the men marveled, saying, "What sort [of person] is this, that even the winds and the sea obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"
en.B: They were amazed. "What kind of person is this?" they said. "Even the winds and the sea obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.R: The followers were amazed. They said, "Who is this man? Even the wind and the waves obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

fr.L: Et les hommes furent dans l’étonnement, disant : « Quel est donc celui-ci, pour que même les vents et la mer {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} obéissent ? »
fr.B: Ils furent stupéfaits. « Qui est donc cet homme ? disaient-ils. Même les vents et la mer {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} obéissent ! »
fr.R: Les disciples ont été très étonnés. Ils ont dit : « Qui est cet homme ? Même le vent et les vagues {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} obéissent ! »

decisions.choice: the men: the people in the boat, the disciples
alternatives: other people who heard the story
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, which may set them against the one whom wind and sea obey.

decisions.choice: what sort of person is this: the question points to God
decisions.reason: In Scripture only God commands the sea (Psalm 89:10; Job 38:8-11). Matthew leaves the question for the reader to answer.

decisions.choice: they (B); the followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the group without the generic "men".

source.text: Καὶ ἐλθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πέραν εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γαδαρηνῶν ὑπήντησαν αὐτῷ δύο δαιμονιζόμενοι ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἐξερχόμενοι, χαλεποὶ λίαν ὥστε μὴ ἰσχύειν τινὰ παρελθεῖν διὰ τῆς ὁδοῦ ἐκείνης.

records.literal_gloss: And having come of him to the other side into the region of the Gadarenes met him two demon-possessed out of the tombs coming, violent very, so that not was able anyone to pass through the way that.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to the other side, to the region of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed [men] met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, coming out of the tombs, extremely violent, so that no one was able to pass by that way.
en.B: When Jesus arrived on the other side, in the region of the Gadarenes, two men controlled by demons came out of the tombs to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were so dangerous that nobody dared to use that road.
en.R: Jesus arrived on the other side of the lake, in the land of the Gadarenes. Two men who had demons in them came out of the burial caves and met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were so dangerous that no one could walk on that road.

fr.L: Et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut arrivé sur l’autre rive, dans le pays des Gadaréniens, deux possédés vinrent à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre, sortant des tombeaux, extrêmement violents, si bien que personne ne pouvait passer par ce chemin-là.
fr.B: Lorsque Jésus arriva sur l’autre rive, dans le pays des Gadaréniens, deux hommes sous l’emprise de démons sortirent des tombeaux et vinrent à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre. Ils étaient si dangereux que personne n’osait passer par ce chemin.
fr.R: Jésus est arrivé de l’autre côté du lac, dans le pays des Gadaréniens. Deux hommes qui avaient des démons en eux sont sortis des grottes où l’on enterrait les morts, et ils sont venus à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre. Ils étaient si dangereux que personne ne pouvait passer par ce chemin.

decisions.choice: Gadarenes, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ over the name, as they do in Mark 5:1 and Luke 8:26. Gadara was a town about six miles southeast of the lake. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: two men
alternatives: one man, as in Mark and Luke
decisions.reason: Mark 5:2 and Luke 8:27 tell of one man. Matthew has two here, as he has two blind men in 20:30; he does not explain.

decisions.choice: the tombs: burial caves, unclean places outside the town
decisions.reason: Tombs were cut into the rock. Living among the dead made a person unclean and cut off.

decisions.choice: burial caves
decisions.reason: Readable describes them.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced names Jesus.

decisions.choice: deux possédés (L), deux hommes sous l’emprise de démons (B), deux hommes qui avaient des démons en eux (R); les tombeaux (L, B), les grottes où l’on enterrait les morts (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:16 and in the French of Mark 5: "démoniaque" now mostly means "fiendish", so Literal says "possédés"; Readable describes the burial caves, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἔκραξαν λέγοντες· Τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: And behold, they cried out saying, What to us and to you, Son of the God?

en.L: And look, they cried out, saying, "What [is there] to us and to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Son of God?
en.B: They screamed, "Son of God, what business do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have with us?
en.R: They shouted, "What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want with us, Son of God?

fr.L: Et voici, ils crièrent, disant : « Qu’[y a-t-il] entre nous et {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, Fils de Dieu ?
fr.B: Ils hurlèrent : « Fils de Dieu, qu’as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} à faire avec nous ?
fr.R: Ils ont crié : « Que nous veux-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, Fils de Dieu ?

decisions.choice: what to us and to you: what do we have in common? Leave us alone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom rejects someone's interference (Judges 11:12; 1 Kings 17:18).

decisions.choice: Son of God: the demons know who Jesus is
decisions.reason: God called Jesus his Son at the baptism (3:17); the tempter knew it (4:3); now the demons cry it out, while the disciples are still asking (8:27).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

source.text: ἦλθες ὧδε πρὸ καιροῦ βασανίσαι ἡμᾶς;

records.literal_gloss: Did you come here before time to torment us?

en.L: Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come here before the time to torment us?"
en.B: Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come here to torment us before the appointed time?"
en.R: Did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come here to punish us before the time God has set?"

fr.L: Es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} venu ici avant le temps pour nous tourmenter ? »
fr.B: Es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} venu ici pour nous tourmenter avant le moment fixé ? »
fr.R: Est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es venu ici pour nous punir avant le moment que Dieu a fixé ? »

decisions.choice: before the time: before the appointed day of judgment
decisions.reason: The demons know their end is set for the final judgment (25:41). They see that end breaking in early with Jesus.

decisions.choice: the time God has set
decisions.reason: Readable says whose time it is.

source.text: ἦν δὲ μακρὰν ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀγέλη χοίρων πολλῶν βοσκομένη.

records.literal_gloss: There was then far from them a herd of pigs many feeding.

en.L: Now far from them a herd of many pigs was feeding.
en.B: Some distance away a large herd of pigs was feeding.
en.R: Some distance away, a big herd of pigs was eating.

fr.L: Or il y avait, loin d’eux, un troupeau de nombreux porcs qui paissait.
fr.B: À quelque distance de là, un grand troupeau de porcs était en train de paître.
fr.R: Un peu plus loin, un grand troupeau de cochons était en train de manger.

decisions.choice: a herd of pigs: in a Gentile region
decisions.reason: The law forbade Jews to eat pork (Leviticus 11:7). A large herd fits the Gentile towns of the Decapolis.

source.text: οἱ δὲ δαίμονες παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Εἰ ἐκβάλλεις ἡμᾶς, ἀπόστειλον ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν ἀγέλην τῶν χοίρων.

records.literal_gloss: The then demons were begging him saying, If you cast out us, send us into the herd of the pigs.

en.L: And the demons begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cast us out, send us into the herd of pigs."
en.B: The demons kept begging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs."
en.R: The demons begged Jesus, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make us leave these men, send us into that herd of pigs."

fr.L: Et les démons {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suppliaient, disant : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous chasses, envoie-nous dans le troupeau de porcs. »
fr.B: Les démons ne cessaient de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} supplier : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous chasses, envoie-nous dans ce troupeau de porcs. »
fr.R: Les démons ont supplié Jésus : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous fais sortir de ces hommes, envoie-nous dans ce troupeau de cochons. »

decisions.choice: begged: kept begging
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures repeated pleading. The demons know they must obey.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Go.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Go."
en.B: "Go!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them.
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Go!"

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Allez. »
fr.B: « Allez ! » leur dit-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}.
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Allez ! »

decisions.choice: Go: one word is enough
decisions.reason: As with the sick (8:8, 16), Jesus's single word is obeyed.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐξελθόντες ἀπῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους· καὶ ἰδοὺ ὥρμησεν πᾶσα ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, καὶ ἀπέθανον ἐν τοῖς ὕδασιν.

records.literal_gloss: They then having come out went into the pigs; and behold, rushed all the herd down the steep bank into the sea, and they died in the waters.

en.L: And they came out and went into the pigs; and look, the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and they died in the waters.
en.B: The demons came out and entered the pigs, and at once the whole herd stampeded down the slope into the lake and drowned.
en.R: The demons left the men and went into the pigs. Then the whole herd ran down the steep hill into the lake and drowned.

fr.L: Et, étant sortis, ils s’en allèrent dans les porcs ; et voici, tout le troupeau se précipita du haut de l’escarpement dans la mer, et ils moururent dans les eaux.
fr.B: Les démons sortirent et entrèrent dans les porcs, et aussitôt tout le troupeau se rua en bas de la pente dans le lac et se noya.
fr.R: Les démons sont sortis des hommes et ils sont entrés dans les cochons. Alors tout le troupeau a couru jusqu’en bas de la colline, qui était très raide. Les cochons sont tombés dans le lac, et ils se sont noyés.

decisions.choice: the herd rushed into the sea: the demons' power to destroy, and its end
decisions.reason: The sea was a picture of chaos and death. The destruction shows what the demons would have done to the men.

decisions.choice: look (L); at once (B); then (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

source.text: οἱ δὲ βόσκοντες ἔφυγον, καὶ ἀπελθόντες εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀπήγγειλαν πάντα καὶ τὰ τῶν δαιμονιζομένων.

records.literal_gloss: The then feeding fled, and having gone into the city they reported all things and the [things] of the demon-possessed.

en.L: And those tending [them] fled, and going into the town they reported everything, including what had happened to the demon-possessed [men].
en.B: The men looking after the pigs ran off into the town and reported everything, including what had happened to the men with demons.
en.R: The men who were taking care of the pigs ran away to the town. They told everyone what had happened, and what had happened to the men who had demons.

fr.L: Et ceux qui les faisaient paître s’enfuirent, et, s’en étant allés dans la ville, ils rapportèrent tout, et ce qui [était arrivé] aux possédés.
fr.B: Les gardiens des porcs s’enfuirent dans la ville et racontèrent tout, y compris ce qui était arrivé aux hommes possédés par les démons.
fr.R: Les hommes qui gardaient les cochons se sont enfuis jusqu’à la ville. Ils ont raconté à tout le monde ce qui s’était passé, et ce qui était arrivé aux hommes qui avaient des démons.

decisions.choice: the town: probably Gadara or a village near the lake
decisions.reason: The word can mean a town of any size.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ πᾶσα ἡ πόλις ἐξῆλθεν εἰς ὑπάντησιν τῷ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν παρεκάλεσαν ὅπως μεταβῇ ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And behold, all the city went out to meet the Jesus, and having seen him they begged that he would depart from the region of them.

en.L: And look, the whole town came out to meet Jesus, and when they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they begged [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] to leave their region.
en.B: At that the whole town came out to meet Jesus, and when they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to go away from their district.
en.R: So all the people of the town came out to meet Jesus. When they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to go away from their land.

fr.L: Et voici, toute la ville sortit à la rencontre de Jésus, et, {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ayant vu, ils [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] supplièrent de s’éloigner de leur territoire.
fr.B: Alors toute la ville sortit à la rencontre de Jésus ; et quand les gens {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} virent, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} supplièrent de quitter leur région.
fr.R: Alors tous les habitants de la ville sont sortis pour aller voir Jésus. Quand ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont vu, ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont supplié de partir de leur pays.

decisions.choice: they begged him to leave: fear and loss outweigh wonder
decisions.reason: The demons begged to go into the pigs; the town begs Jesus to go away. Matthew does not say why, but the loss of the herd and fear of his power fit the story.

decisions.choice: look (L); at that (B); so (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.
